overview: Handle common objections after presenting damage. Create urgency, use evidence, and maintain momentum toward the contingency and claim filing.
learningObjectives: Use evidence and education to reassure
Leverage contingency protection to move forward

sections.title: Common Objections
sections.content: Rates will go up; Damage doesn’t look bad; Need to think about it; Want a second opinion; Don’t want insurance hassle. Use evidence (photos, granules), education (weather claims), and contingency protections.

sections.title: Advanced Techniques
sections.content: Acknowledge & validate; Provide evidence; Create urgency (storms are time‑sensitive); Offer reassurance and options.

activities.title: Objection Drill
activities.description: Practice responding to 3 objections in a row.

prompts.expectedResponse: Educate weather vs. at‑fault; value of policy

agnesContent.title: Keep Momentum
points: Offer alternatives and schedule next step

quiz.question: How to respond to ‘damage doesn’t look bad’?
quiz.correctAnswer: Explain long‑term effects (freeze‑thaw, leaks) and show collateral evidence.

quiz.question: What evidence supports storm causation?
quiz.correctAnswer: Granule accumulation, soft metals dents, screen pitting, directional wind patterns.
